The ISIS lure

By: Bernadette Maguire | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Are young South African girls being lured to join ISIS with false promises? And we ask is this part of a growing global trend?

Summary:
This week it was revealed that a 15 year old South African girl narrowly escaped ISIS recruitment. She's not alone. A young PE girl was also caught by her family at OR Tambo on route to Syria via Turkey. Another young Bela Bela girl is allegedly already there along with 2 PE families who left lock stock and barrel. The Iraqi ambassador in SA is on the record stating that around 140 South African's have joined ISIS.

We speak to a family member of one of the PE families, the lawyer and spokeswoman for the young PE girl and to Yusuf Abramjee who helped to locate and rescue the Cape Town girl.

Then, with the help of a 19 year old Muslim girl, we explore the platforms and the recruitment process that lures young girls making it appear like they will be joining the ultimate liberated utopia. Social media platforms are used to do this - she will create a fake profile and then share the propaganda that is used to lure her.

We are also able to access 20 videos that ISIS released - all these videos have been subjected to rigorous video analysis by the Florida based TRAC team.

Bigger picture: we will speak to leading Muslim thinkers and clerics about the level of support for ISIS within SA within the context of who ISIS is and who they purport to represent. There was an article in today's Times alleging that Muslim clerics were being threatened for speaking out against the Islamic state terrorist organisation.

Further information:
The PE family of the Desai girl say they are not prepared to speak and that the young girl is still trying to go. They are keeping a close eye on her. Apparently she tried to use her sisters passport to get out of the country, supposedly on the advice of the recruiters on the other side.

However, the family spokesman or her lawyer - Yasmeen who works with Omar can speak to us - the family has given permission. We spoke to Yasmeen yesterday and she's a very articulate beautiful Muslim woman and I think would give a great interview and insights.She spoke at length about the allure of ISIS and having gone to the sites and the recruitment videos it does appear to be a form of utopia for young Muslim women. What they don't tell you is that you can never leave and if you try you are killed. Step out of line and you are dead. I'll send you the links shortly. The video is in English and is very good quality.

I also think our viewers would be very interested in hearing the ISIS story and having a Muslim perspective which is sorely lacking in mainstream media. In fact most of our viewers see ISIS merely as a terror group somewhere in the middle east who behead journalists. We could flesh that story out dramatically and give a greater understanding of who they are and how they operate, They are very organised - have admin staff, pro's. social media people, medical staff, families and fighters.

Press Release:


The lure of Isis
Last week a 15-year-old South African girl narrowly escaped ISIS recruitment. She is one of many Western teenagers lured to Syria through the group’s powerful online propaganda machine. Experts say ISIS has especially ramped up its efforts to lure young women. Could terror groups be trying to recruit South African children through social media? Carte Blanche investigates.


Script:


The Isis Lure - Script


Narcissism to another level VO: 29”
The name Isis instills fear in the hearts of people around the globe and yet the Islamic extremist group is growing.

Infamous for public beheadings and executions they kill indiscriminately in a war waged in the name of creating an Islamic state in Syria and Iraq.

Under the leadership of Abu Bakr Al-Baghdadi their call to arms has become more sophisticated with the release of recruitment videos aimed at convincing foreign nationals to join the jihad or holy war.

Abu Muthanna Al Yemeni:
What gives you life is jihad - we have brothers from Bangladesh, from Iraqi, from Cambodia, Australia, UK.


VO: 11”
This unprecedented recruitment campaign nearly netted a 15 year old Cape Town teen recently – if it wasn’t for swift action from Crimeline’s Yusuf Abramjee who received a distress call.

?
Yusuf:
A 15 year girl had gone missing and her family required help.

VO: 4
Her grandfather confirmed her passport and money was gone.

Yusuf:
He said to me that he suspected it could be linked to ISIS because some documents had been found in her room.

VO: 6.5
Yusuf immediately raised the alarm on social media and alerted the State Security Agency and Crime Intelligence.

Yusuf:
At about half past five a Colonel called me from the police in the Western Cape saying they had managed to trace the girl, she was on board a British airways domestic flight. They took her off the flight, took her in for brief questioning at the police station at the airport, before being transferred to Cape Town for further questioning bylaw enforcement agencies.


VO: 13
She’s not the first South African teen trying to make her way to Syria lawyer Zehir Omar who is aware of two others – one from PE and another from Bela Bela. The PE girl managed to get as far as Joburg.

Zehir:
When she landed in OR Tambo there were some glitches, with her flight to Turkey, glitches in the sense that she needed money or some other resource. The parents then found out, they contacted members of the family, went to the airport and dissuaded the girl from continuing her journey.

VO: 14.5
The PE teenager apparently stole her sisters’ passport and planned to fly on that. The young girl from Bela Bela managed to slip past the authorities as did 2 PE families says Muslim woman’s organization leader Yasmin Omar.




Yasmin:
Two entire families from PE also succumbed to the call for Isis, believing that they are joining a noble Islamic cause and that they are bringing relief to muslims across the world.


Devi:
With children?

Yasmin:
With children, wife, husband all have left already.

VO: 11.5
They left a middle class home behind and it’s feared they have signed up to be cannon fodder. 3 SA’s have already been killed in combat says the Iraqi ambassador to SA – Dr Hishan Al-Alawi.


Hisham:
We obviously managed to get their details, how they managed to go there, who was responsible for their recruitment, unfortunately they were killed while fighting for those groups.

VO: 9
With the number of foreign fighters swelling daily – numbers have risen from 7000 in February 2014 to more than 25 000 today.

All sold on the premise that martyrdom will be rewarded with heaven. Hisham:
That global trend together with the fact that Isis and other groups have been using very sophisticated and robust recruitment methods to attract and recruit people.

VO: 5”
They’re lured in videos by promises that martyrdom comes with huge rewards.

Abu Dujana Al Hindi:
Know that if you fear death and that’s what prevents you death will reach you anyway. It will be more painful for you than for the Shehada. The Shehada they don’t feel death except like a sting of an insect.

VO: 11.5
The most potent tool in their recruitment arsenal – social media. Layla, a young muslim woman showed us a popular meme used to convince young women that they’ll be joining an empowered Muslim society.

Layla:
They’re basically painting a perfect picture for you, like a fairy tale, happy ending. But its not like that. It doesn’t make sense if you have it here why would you go there. The only difference is that you are holding a gun.

VO: 12
On facebook and blogs young woman are promised homes, husbands, food, medical care and an allowance 700 dollars a month. It’s done clandestinely – there are no application forms.

Layla
It’ your social circle – you know a friend knows a friend and that’s how you can get information.

VO: 10”
Secretary general of the muslim council of theologians, Moulana Ebrahim Bham says they’ve issued statements but now, in a rare move, need to take the message into cyberspace.

Ebrahim:
The challenge is now not only to speak in sermons but to reach out to them where they congregate, maybe to reach out to them in the communications which they are accustomed to.

Devi Social media?

Ebrahim:
Social media.

VO: 5”
It’s critical because reality on the ground is a far cry from the online promises.

Zehir:
Isis may be likened to an organization of horror, lies and deceit. It is without doubt a terrorist organization.

Yasmin:
It’s nothing like what was promised to them. There is no husband waiting for them, there is no home that they are going to occupy. In fact they are kept together in a compound, given firearms and told to go out and do battle.

VO: 9
And yet the online propaganda is very convincing. Goolam and Zunaid, two university students, say they nearly signed up.

Devi:
Did you feel attracted to it? Did you feel that this is something you can identify with?

Goolam:
To a certain extent yes Islamically. We understood what they were saying according to us and what we believed going to Muslim schools, why they were doing what they were doing.

VO: 4.5
They say watching Isis videos online inspired them to join the battle.

Devi:
If you were given the invitation to go and see what was going on, on the explicit understanding that if you didn’t like it you could leave and come back. Would you go?

Goolam:
Yes I would go.

Devi:
In a heartbeat?

Goolam and Zunaid:
Yes in a heartbeat.

VO: 8.5
But liberal theologians like Prof Farid Esack believes that Isis is misleading the youth and that their ethos contravenes the strict teachings of the Qu’ran.

Farid:
I think that they are justifying it in a very decontextualized manner, they are taking those texts in isolation and are quite literally using those texts as weapons in their own armoury.

VO: 14
For instance, the recruiters call to woman to travel alone and join the war is itself haram or forbidden. But for teenagers like Goolam the mixed messages, distrust in the media and a western agenda have created confusion and uncertainty.

Goolam:
The thing is with media, how I feel is that, media has been twisted and shaped in such a way that you see what they want you to see. So I don’t know what to believe now and the problem is now, our curiosity is that I am tired of seeing what they want me to see and I want to go there now and see what’s actually going on.

VO: 4.5
Prof Esack puts it down to the youthful search for identity and meaning.

Farid:
I think that Isis offers some theatrics and drama and so on. I think that very often young people want out of something, without asking sufficient questions about into what?


VO: 13”
These are the vulnerabilities that the ISIS puppet masters play on in a complex political game. The Iraqi ambassador believes that after Saddam Hussein was ousted in 2003 – Isis filled a vacuum and found fertile ground.

Hisham:
They wanted to use this tool to make people realize that the change is not going to produce meaningful outcomes, ie whatever was there in Iraq before 2003 regardless of the criticism was better than the outcome that they are going to see.

VO: 1
To fund their campaign analysts claim they sell between 1 and 3 million dollars worth of oil on the black market daily. It’s this money that fuels the propaganda machine. Spiritual leaders need to create a strong counter.

Yusuf:
The time has now come for us to now educate the community at large about the dangers of Isis, making sure that we don’t use the indoctrination that these people are using to try to recruit people.

Zehir:
Some time could be devotes to tell the congregation – beware of a group that calls themselves Isis. This group purports to advance the interests of Muslims and they are not – they are a fraud – they are liars. Their very call to join combat goes against
Sharia and the Qu’ran.




Devi link
You’d be wrong if you think that this issue only concerns Muslims – it concerns every South African.

Yasmin:
It’s not only Muslim people that are responding to the call from Isis – we have people from various sectors of society, we’ve had Scottish women, American women who are not necessarily Muslims responding to the call.

VO 6”
But apart from the threat to our people, the volatility in the oil fields could impact on our pockets at the pumps.

Zehir:
If the conflict in the middle east expands, if the conflict increasesoil will not be able to leave, and if oil cannot leave then the price will become astronomical.

VO: 5.5
Fortunately experts believe ISIS does not pose a terror threat on the ground in South Africa,

Hisham:
We are not talking about Daaish or Isis or other groups coming here of starting their bombing attacks here, they are as you rightly indicate, more interested in recruiting men and women and using them in various ways in Syria or Iraq including using them to recruit more men and women.

VO:9.5
We’d hate to see more of our youth lost to war mongering by a terror group which many believe is based on nothing more than false ideologies and narcissism.


Promo 1:

VO: 10”
Why would teenagers from middle class homes risk everything to join terror group Isis in war torn Syria – we sift through propaganda and promises.


Promo 2:

VO: 8
As extremist group Isis’s army swells to over 200 000 their recruitment campaign is starting to find resonance with some South African teens.

Farid:
Often young people want out of something without asking sufficient questions of into what?


Promo 3:

VO: 10
Extremist group Isis use religion to whip up public sentiment to recruit foreigners – but once there its alleged they are nothing more than cannon fodder.

Yasmin:
…told to go out and do battle.









VO:
The 15 year old’s attempt to leave a comfortable middle class life to join a brutal war has left more questions than answers.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Are young South African girls being lured to join ISIS with false promises? And we ask is this part of a growing global trend?
metadata.Summary: This week it was revealed that a 15 year old South African girl narrowly escaped ISIS recruitment. She's not alone. A young PE girl was also caught by her family at OR Tambo on route to Syria via Turkey. Another young Bela Bela girl is allegedly already there along with 2 PE families who left lock stock and barrel. The Iraqi ambassador in SA is on the record stating that around 140 South African's have joined ISIS. We speak to a family member of one of the PE families, the lawyer and spokeswoman for the young PE girl and to Yusuf Abramjee who helped to locate and rescue the Cape Town girl. Then, with the help of a 19 year old Muslim girl, we explore the platforms and the recruitment process that lures young girls making it appear like they will be joining the ultimate liberated utopia. Social media platforms are used to do this - she will create a fake profile and then share the propaganda that is used to lure her. We are also able to access 20 videos that ISIS released - all these videos have been subjected to rigorous video analysis by the Florida based TRAC team. Bigger picture: we will speak to leading Muslim thinkers and clerics about the level of support for ISIS within SA within the context of who ISIS is and who they purport to represent. There was an article in today's Times alleging that Muslim clerics were being threatened for speaking out against the Islamic state terrorist organisation.
metadata.Further information: The PE family of the Desai girl say they are not prepared to speak and that the young girl is still trying to go. They are keeping a close eye on her. Apparently she tried to use her sisters passport to get out of the country, supposedly on the advice of the recruiters on the other side. However, the family spokesman or her lawyer - Yasmeen who works with Omar can speak to us - the family has given permission. We spoke to Yasmeen yesterday and she's a very articulate beautiful Muslim woman and I think would give a great interview and insights.She spoke at length about the allure of ISIS and having gone to the sites and the recruitment videos it does appear to be a form of utopia for young Muslim women. What they don't tell you is that you can never leave and if you try you are killed. Step out of line and you are dead. I'll send you the links shortly. The video is in English and is very good quality. I also think our viewers would be very interested in hearing the ISIS story and having a Muslim perspective which is sorely lacking in mainstream media. In fact most of our viewers see ISIS merely as a terror group somewhere in the middle east who behead journalists. We could flesh that story out dramatically and give a greater understanding of who they are and how they operate, They are very organised - have admin staff, pro's. social media people, medical staff, families and fighters.
